items.title: EU expands migration cooperation with eastern Libya through new funding
items.description: The European Union has signed an additional €25 million ($29 million) in funding to expand migration cooperation into eastern Libya, according to a letter from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to EU leaders, seen by Reuters. The funding will support border management, search-and-rescue and anti-smuggling activities in eastern Libya. It is a further sign of deepening EU engagement with the region controlled by military commander Khalifa Haftar ​, as Brussels seeks to curb irregular migration across the Mediterranean. Libya, ⁠where control is split between rival western and eastern administrations, has ​been a major transit route for migrants attempting the dangerous sea crossing ​to Europe since the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled Muammar Gaddafi . The EU and its member states have long supported and trained the Libyan coast guard, which intercepts migrants at sea. While the EU formally recognises only the Tripoli-based government, ​it has stepped up contacts with authorities in eastern Libya since last year ‌as ⁠migrant departures from areas controlled by Haftar in eastern Libya have risen. The move follows the EU’s July announcement that it would establish a Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in the eastern Libyan city of Benghazi, further expanding cooperation with authorities in the east. “Libya remains the top country of departure for illegal crossings to the EU,” von der ​Leyen wrote, describing an upcoming EU-Libya meeting as a ​way ⁠to keep cooperation going. She said the EU and the International Organisation for Migration were supporting voluntary returns from Libya to countries of origin. “We are ⁠equally ​focused on reducing the number of migrants ​arriving in Libya with the sole intention of crossing illegally into the EU,” she ​added.

items.title: Libya: Eastern Authorities Carry Out Wave of Executions
items.description: Click to expand Image Military leader of Eastern Libya, Khalifa Haftar (center), attends a conference in Sabha, Libya, September 5, 2024. © 2024 Khaled Nasraoui/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Photo (Beirut) – The Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), which controls eastern and southern Libya, has executed at least 31 people since late August 2026 following grossly unfair military trials, Human Rights Watch said today. These are the first known executions in Libya since 2010, with at least 50 more people in Gernada military prison at imminent risk of execution. On August 23, the LAAF military prosecutor announced that 10 people had been executed by firing squad after being convicted of murder and terrorism-related offenses. Human rights groups have documented a total of at least 31 executions as of September 10. The LAAF, led by General Khalifa Haftar, should immediately halt all executions and impose a moratorium on the death penalty, Human Rights Watch said. “The Libyan Arab Armed Forces are putting people to death after secret trials built on confessions allegedly extracted through torture, in courts that Libya’s own Supreme Court has said should not be trying civilians,” said Bassam Khawaja, deputy Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “Every execution carried out under these conditions is an irreversible injustice and every government with influence over the LAAF should be pressing hard to stop the next one.” Many of those executed had been arrested in the cities of Derna and Benghazi during or after the armed conflict between the LAAF and opposing armed groups between 2014 and 2018. Between 2018 and 2021, military courts in eastern Libya convicted hundreds of civilians in secret trials targeting real or perceived critics of the LAAF, sentencing at least 22 to death. According to Amnesty International, many of the sentences were based on confessions allegedly extracted under torture by the Internal Security Agency, an LAAF-affiliated armed group. At least two death sentences were reduced to life in prison on appeal by a higher military court in 2019, yet the defendants were put to death this year regardless. The executions also went ahead despite a November 2025 ruling by the constitutional chamber of Libya’s Supreme Court that Law No. 4/2017 is unconstitutional insofar as it grants military courts jurisdiction to try civilians for terrorism and crimes against the state. Local human rights groups said that the military trials violated defendants’ due process rights. They were held in secret and without prior notice. Defendants’ families, journalists, and human rights organizations were not allowed to attend. Several defendants were denied lawyers of their choice and those who did have their own lawyers were refused visits before and during trial and could not speak with them privately. They were apparently not allowed to present their cases in court or examine the evidence against them. The verdicts were handed down without providing the defendants or their attorneys with written and reasoned judgments. Trying civilians in military courts is incompatible with the right to a fair trial under human rights law and such trials violate the right to be tried before an independent and impartial tribunal. In Libya, military prosecutors are often not qualified to investigate civilians and they lack independence. The military prosecutors and judges in eastern Libya are themselves affiliated with the LAAF or allied armed groups. Families of defendants were not notified in advance that the executions would take place. The authorities refused to hand over the bodies of those executed, asked relatives to confirm the identities of the dead, then buried them without families present and warned relatives not to hold funerals. Secret executions and denying families a last visit violate international law, including by inflicting severe mental suffering on those executed and their relatives in breach of the absolute prohibition of torture and other ill-treatment. Libya remains split between two rival authorities. The Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU), which is internationally recognized, controls the west, alongside affiliated security agencies and armed groups. The LAAF and affiliated forces and militias control the east and south. Both sides operate with near-total impunity. The United Nations and the GNU condemned the executions. Governments that fund, train, and legitimize the LAAF have real leverage, and a responsibility to use it, publicly and privately, to press LAAF leaders to halt all executions, Human Rights Watch said. Libya’s justice sector is fragmented and deeply polarized. Human Rights Watch has previously documented outdated and repressive legislation, a lack of fair trial rights, and rampant due process violations. Unaccountable militias control prisons that are only nominally under state ministries. Libyan authorities in both the east and west should restrict the jurisdiction of military courts to military offenses committed by military personnel and stop trying civilians in military courts altogether. They should promptly review all cases of civilians wrongfully detained and prosecuted before military courts and provide effective remedies, including release, transfer to civilian courts, or retrial in line with international fair trial standards, with acknowledgment of time served. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all countries and under all circumstances because it is inherently inhumane, uniquely cruel and irreversible, and universally plagued by arbitrariness, prejudice, and error. Ninety-two countries have ratified a protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights that requires the abolition of the death penalty, recognizing that capital punishment violates the right to life and the prohibition of cruel, inhuman, or degrading punishment. Libya should abolish the death penalty and until then enact a moratorium on all executions. “Libya went more than 15 years without an execution, and the LAAF has shattered that moratorium in a matter of weeks,” Khawaja said. “The lives of at least 50 more people now depend on whether Haftar’s forces, and the governments that back them, choose to stop this.”

items.title: European Governments Fall Short on Reparatory Justice
items.description: Click to expand Image Secretary-General António Guterres addresses the 55th session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva, Switzerland, February 26, 2024. © 2024 Elma Okic/UN Photo A United Nations Human Rights Council resolution on October 7 calling for concrete action against systemic racism should have been an opportunity for governments to demonstrate their commitment to racial justice. Instead, the United Kingdom called for a vote, breaking from last year’s consensus on the annually tabled resolution. Citing concerns about the applicability of international law to establish responsibility and accountability for colonial harm, the UK objected to language on reparations and then abstained from the vote; European Union members of the Council also abstained. Regardless, the resolution passed with 30 votes in favor, 17 abstentions, and none against. The loss of last year’s consensus reveals the gap between the UK and other European governments’ stated dedication to combat racism and their actual political willingness to address its historical roots. European governments have present-day obligations to tackle racial discrimination and provide effective remedies. The International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination requires states, including the UK, to ensure just and adequate reparation for harm resulting from racial discrimination. The experts who monitor this treaty earlier this year set out clear legal guidance on states’ obligations for such reparation. Enslavement and colonialism helped establish racial inequalities, the consequences of which persist today. Human Rights Watch has documented systemic racism, including racial profiling and barriers to economic and social rights in Europe. Reparatory justice is essential to confronting these enduring harms. Jamaica’s pursuit of an advisory opinion from the Judicial Committee of the UK’s Privy Council underscores the importance of examining governments’ legal arguments. Its petition asks whether the enslavement of Africans was lawful under English and international law, and whether the UK owes a reparatory remedy. Next month’s Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda offers another opportunity to change course. King Charles’s forthcoming Caribbean visit will, apparently, include an acknowledgement of Britain’s involvement in enslavement, although Buckingham Palace says decisions on reparations and formal apologies rest with the UK government. The UK and other European governments should engage meaningfully with African and Caribbean initiatives and affected communities to develop reparatory measures for the harms they were and are responsible for. These measures can include, according to UN principles, compensation, restitution, rehabilitation, acknowledgment of wrongdoing and reforms to prevent recurrence. Affected communities should shape the process and its outcomes. The United Nations Human Rights Council resolution calls on governments to move “from rhetoric to reality.” Those that are serious about ending systemic racism should embrace reparatory justice as part of that work.

items.title: Actress Selma Blair faces charges for kicking nurse and officer after plane incident
items.description: US actress Selma Blair has been charged with two additional assault counts over allegedly kicking an officer and a nurse after being removed from a flight. Blair was arrested late Sunday in New York after she allegedly attacked flight attendants on a Delta plane travelling from Los Angeles to New York. The FBI issued her a federal summons accusing her of assault on board. While appearing in court over the additional charges, the Legally Blonde star’s attorney asked the judge to consider the actress’s “body of work”, and called Blair the “gold standard.” The judge said she should not “get special treatment”. Blair has pleaded not guilty. She has since been released on bail. She was taken to hospital after the incident on the flight. Her representatives have told the BBC that she had “experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct”. As the flight landed in New York on Sunday evening, airport officials responded to a call about “a physically abusive passenger” on the flight. Two flight attendants were hurt, and one was taken to hospital, the New York Port Authority said. Audio recorded on air traffic control details a pilot asking for medical help, describing “a bloody nose” and “some bite marks”, according to CBS News, BBC’s US News partner. Blair, 54, who also starred in Cruel Intentions and Hellboy, was arrested and taken to hospital. She was issued a federal summons for a charge of assault within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the US. The two additional charges of assault, filed in state court, came after she was taken off the plane. One of the alleged assaults happened when she was being transported in an ambulance, where she allegedly kicked a police officer. Once at the hospital, prosecutors allege that she also assaulted a nurse. At her arraignment in Queens, Blair’s attorney Shawn Barnes asked the judge for leniency. He said that “violence” is “not who she is” and asked for the judge to consider her body of work. The actress is somebody that people look up to, he said, referring to her as “the gold standard”. The judge denied his request, saying she “should not get special treatment…because she is a celebrity”. The judge set her bail at $20,000 cash or $60,000 bond, with the next hearing scheduled for 19 January. It is unclear when a date will be set for the federal case against her, which concerns the allegations of assault aboard the aircraft.

items.title: Online abuse puts 1.5m Pakistani children at risk: study
items.description: WASHINGTON: About 1.5 million internet-using children in Pakistan experienced sexual exploitation or abuse facilitated by digital technology in a single year, according to new research, as a senior United Nations official warns that artificial intelligence and overlapping global crises are creating new dangers for children. Presenting her final report to the UN General Assembly on Monday, Najat Maalla M’jid, the secretary general’s Special Representative on Violence Against Children, urged governments to strengthen protections for children facing multiple and overlapping crises. “Almost 45 million children are displaced because of conflict, but also because of natural disasters, because of the climate crisis,” she told journalists at UN Headquarters in New York. Rapid advances in technology are creating new risks alongside opportunities for children to learn and communicate. Artificial intelligence has opened what Ms M’jid described as “huge avenues for child sexual exploitation”, as well as “cyberbullying, deepfakes and the recruitment of children into criminal activities.” Her presentation marked 20 years since the first UN global study on violence against children. Despite progress, she warned, the world continued to face complex and overlapping crises in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. Troubling picture Nearly one in 16 internet-using children aged 12 to 17 in Pakistan — approximately 1.5 million children — experienced at least one form of technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse in a single year, according to Disrupting Harm in Pakistan, a study published by Unicef, ECPAT International and INTERPOL in September 2026. The UN General Assembly on Monday identified AI-generated sexual material as an emerging risk. The abuses include unwanted sexual images or conversations, demands for intimate photographs, the non-consensual sharing of children’s images, and sexual threats or blackmail. The findings challenge the perception that online abuse is mainly perpetrated by strangers. In 85 per cent of the incidents cited by ch­­­­­­i­­­l­­dren, the perpetrator was someone they alre­ady knew. Social media accounted for 44pc of reported instances of abuse, making it the most commonly reported digital setting. Fear, stigma and possible repercussions at home often prevent children from seeking help. Victims may fear being blamed, humiliated or subjected to restrictions by their families. Boys, too, risk being overlooked because of social expectations about masculinity and the reluctance to discuss sexual abuse. Unicef says more than half of children who experienced technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse did not tell anyone. None of the children surveyed reported their experiences through formal channels such as helplines, social workers or the police. These findings highlight the need for safe, confidential and accessible reporting systems, as well as support that allows children to seek help without fear of blame or punishment. Poverty and displacement Online abuse is part of a wider child-protection challenge shaped by poverty, displacement and disrupted access to essential services. Ms M’jid warned that poverty, food insecurity and rising prices were deepening children’s vulnerability worldwide. Economic hardship can expose children to exploitation, while conflict and natural disasters can disrupt education and weaken family support systems. Climate-related emergencies add to these pressures across South Asia. Unicef estimates that weather-related disasters displaced 15.6m children in the region between 2016 and 2022. In Bangladesh, climate-related events disrupted schooling for 35m children in 2024. These figures concern different as­­p­­­ects of children’s vulnerability; th­­­­ey do not establish a direct link bet­w­­een displacement and online sexual abuse. They nevertheless underline the importance of maintaining child-protection services during emergencies and ensuring that vulnerable families can access support. For Pakistan, the challenge is to address both the risks created by digital technologies and the social and economic circumstances that can leave children without adequate protection. The Pakistani study identifies we­­a­­­k­­­­n­­esses in the systems intended to pr­­­e­­­­­­v­­ent online abuse, investigate cas­es and support victims. Children ne­­­­­­­­ed safe and accessible ways to rep­ort abuse, while investigations must be conducted by appropriately train­­ed personnel. Victims must also be able to obtain support without being exposed to further humiliation or trauma. The study identifies gaps in Pakistan’s legal framework. Legisl­ation does not require child forensic interviews to be systematically conducted by specially trained professionals, increasing the risk of secondary victimisation during investigations. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: A perfect storm
items.description: SOME statements by the ruling party leaders hailing the decision to impose a state of emergency and governor’s rule in KP bring to mind the words of a political leader following the military operation in East Pakistan in 1971: “Thank God, Pakistan is saved.” In fact, that action led to the separation of the eastern wing. Indeed, comparing the two situations may not be correct. Still, such reckless action against a provincial government that holds a two-thirds majority in the assembly could provoke a combustible environment, further destabilising a country that is facing multiple challenges on both the internal and external fronts. For some time, it had been apparent that the hybrid set-up had opted for what is sometimes described as the ‘nuclear option’, as tensions between Islamabad and Peshawar heightened over the PTI’s threat to march on Islamabad. The capital was sealed off with containers, and the highways leading to the city were blocked. Hopes of ending the stand-off arose earlier this month when the government and the opposition agreed to talk. But even a marathon meeting and back-channel contacts failed to break the stalemate. Despite the blame game, it was clear the powers that be were not prepared to agree to the PTI’s major demand — a meeting with Imran Khan — or to implement the orders of the Islamabad High Court and the Supreme Court. While the differences were purely political, the government maintained that the talks broke down over the PTI provincial government’s refusal to cooperate on counterterrorism operations. Some federal ministers declared the PTI government to be an extension of the TTP. The PTI and the provincial government indeed have no clear view regarding the rising cases of terrorism in the province. Still, the party was willing to cooperate provided it was allowed to give its input in any policy. None of it was beyond resolution once the political issues were settled. According to Maulana Fazlur Rahman, who was asked to mediate at the last moment, the PTI was ready to call off its protest march if the government allowed it a meeting with its detained leader. But before his shuttle diplomacy could reach any conclusion, the government imposed a state of emergency in KP, shutting the door on any political solution. The talks seem to have been a mere cover for the crackdown. The protest march that paralysed the province, along with defiant speeches by a novice chief minister, gave the centre justification for the extreme action it took. Without a popular political base, it will not be easy to run a volatile region. In fact, the province was already under unannounced governor’s rule before the formal announcement. While the chief minister led the protest march, the chief secretary and police chief took orders from the governor and Islamabad. Some KP cabinet members and legislators were picked up without the provincial government’s permission. The governor now rules the province, and an indefinite state of emergency has been declared. The provincial government is dissolved, and the non-functional chief minister, Sohail Afridi, and some of his cabinet colleagues have been detained. Indications are that Afridi and some other local PTI leaders could be tried for their alleged involvement in the May 9 attacks and disqualified. Meanwhile, an 11-member advisory council, comprising mostly technocrats, has been installed to run the administration, overseen by Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar. But the real power, though, lies with the establishment. This isn’t the first time an elected provincial government has been sent packing. Still, such swe­­eping action against a government that enjo­yed a two-thirds majority in the assembly has not been seen in recent history. Without a popular political base, it will not be easy to run the administration of a highly volatile region in the midst of resurgent terrorism and a hostile border. There may have been no immediate public reaction to the government’s removal and the crackdown on its leaders, but the tension is palpable. The containers may have been removed in Islamabad, but Peshawar is now barricaded to protect government offices and installations. Educational institutions are closed, and internet services have yet to be restored in many places. The eerie lull speaks of a gathering storm. Governing a highly politicised region from Islamabad or Rawalpindi cannot deliver the desired result, and using force could fuel anger. Most concerning is that it could lead to an unholy alliance between alienated PTI workers and the TTP in troubled districts, compounding the country’s internal security challenges. A fragmented political party can pose a greater threat to internal security. It is a ticking time bomb. What happened in KP is an extension of the authoritarianism trend in the country. The removal of an elected government headed by a party that still enjoys massive popular support, not only in the province but across the country, despite continuing state persecution, will further destabilise the situation. Some federal ministers’ claims that emergency rule has saved KP, as well as Pakistan, are misplaced. The reckless action has further weakened a federal government of questionable legitimacy. Voices already say the present system cannot deliver. They are also calling for a reset of the redundant system. The fault line within the hybrid rule is widening. Emergency rule in KP seems to be the first step towards the resetting of the system — something that has repeatedly been echoed by a minister with strong ties to the establishment. That projected resetting is not meant to restore democracy but to reinforce authoritarianism. With the judiciary constrained by the 26th and 27th Amendments that were rubber-stamped by a compliant parliament, and with various laws curbing freedom of expression, the path towards greater authoritarian rule seems set. We are witnessing a transition from hybrid to hard rule. It is a perfect storm. The writer is an author and journalist. zhussain100@yahoo.com X: @hidhussain Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: La anomalía de la orden del Supremo que solo permite votar a los nacionalizados por la ‘ley de nietos’ que viven en España
items.description: La decisión de Tribunal Supremo de suspender el derecho al voto de los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos deja un reguero de situaciones anómalas a mes y medio de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. La primera y fundamental, la existencia de 163.020 españoles inscritos en el censo a los que se les ha retirado el derecho a votar por un procedimiento en el que no se les ha dado audiencia. Pero de esa medida general brotan otras situaciones paradójicas como la de españoles nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria Democrática de 2022 que votaron en las generales de 2023 o en cualquiera de las autonómicas celebradas desde entonces y a los que ahora se les prohíbe hacerlo; hijos o nietos de exiliados por razones políticas a los que el propio Supremo reconoce el derecho al voto, pero que no van a poder participar en las elecciones porque los consulados no tienen medios para expedir el certificado que requiere el tribunal; y también hay una paradoja sobre la que ni el PP ni Vox ni el Supremo han puesto el foco: españoles que obtuvieron la nacionalidad por la ley de nietos , pero viven en España y votan en cualquiera de las 52 circunscripciones españolas. items.title: ¿Recuerdas lo último que hiciste antes de morir?
items.description: Bryan Cranston ( Breaking Bad) no se ha resistido al humanísimo impulso de despedirse de alguien recordando su último contacto , en este caso RJ Mitte, el actor con parálisis cerebral que interpretó a su hijo en la serie. La incredulidad (Mitte se ha suicidado a los 34 años) tiene muchas maneras de expresarse, pero ninguna mejor que la de contar los planes que teníais con el muerto. “¡Hace unos días quedamos para cenar!”, decimos de uno. “Si hace poco fuimos a jugar al tenis, ¿cómo es posible?”, decimos de otro. De nuestra sorpresa se deduce una conclusión ridícula: “¿Cómo se le ha ocurrido morir si teníamos pensado cenar: nunca piensa en los demás?“, o “¿cómo se pudo haber muerto si jugamos hace poco al tenis, tan mal jugué?”. Cranston relató que hacía poco había intercambiado correos con Mitte para almorzar. Al recordar Cranston su último contacto con él, al recordar nosotros la última vez que vimos a alguien de quien nos dicen que ha muerto de forma sorpresiva, lo que hacemos no es recordar esa última vez, porque para nosotros no era la última cuando lo vimos, no sabíamos que no lo volveríamos a ver, aquello no fue un final ni nada, generalmente se trató de una chorrada sin importancia (“me dijo que iba a votar a la Chunta”) sino que expresamos el íntimo asombro de que nuestro último encuentro fuese algo tan banal, tan parte de la vida como la decena de encuentros casuales que uno va teniendo durante la semana. “No me dijo que iba a tener un infarto en unos días, sólo que estaba acabando de leer un libro de autoayuda”. Pero de pronto lo trivial es trascendente, la muerte da al pasado un significado a veces extraño y ridículo que nos empeñamos en ver sublime (“algo le noté en la mirada cuando me dijo que no volvería a comer panceta”) porque no asumimos o no queremos asumir que la muerte generalmente, si llega de golpe, si llega en tromba, es un acto tan sencillo y despojado de épica como echar la llave. Por eso a menudo la sorpresa de verdad no es que el otro haya muerto, sino que tú no: “Pero cómo ha podido pasar, si me lo encontré hace unos días en el mercado..., y él me encontró a mí”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los buitres son buenas personas
items.description: Los buitres de verdad son buena gente. Da gusto verlos volar por encima del desfiladero de La Yecla, situado junto a Santo Domingo de Silos, o posarse para observar el paisaje desde los cercanos riscos de las Peñas de Cervera. Con sus alas sin aleteo descubrimos la fuerza del viento y el flujo de las corrientes, el movimiento de lo inmóvil. Cuando se posan, conforman un majestuoso ejército limpiador de cadáveres de animales y de sus bacterias; son la funeraria del ecosistema. Y jamás nos atacarán si estamos vivos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El PSOE se aferra a la España periférica para reducir la ventaja de PP y Vox
items.description: El PSOE ha vuelto a depositar casi todas sus esperanzas electorales en la llamada España periférica que ya acudió al rescate de Pedro Sánchez en las elecciones generales de 2023 . Pero esta vez la fortaleza en su gran bastión de Cataluña y la buena respuesta en otras comunidades como Comunidad Valenciana, País Vasco, Canarias, Baleares y Navarra ya no es suficiente para que los socialistas contengan al bloque de las derechas, con el PP estancado pero con Vox disparado en las encuestas . Si hace tres años sumaron 170 diputados entre la derecha tradicional y la ultraderecha (137 y 33) frente a los 152 del PSOE con Sumar (121 y 31), la última encuesta de 40.dB otorga una holgada mayoría absoluta conservadora de 198 escaños (132 y 66). El resto de casas de encuestas, más allá del CIS, presagian un escenario parecido, con Santiago Abascal de vicepresidente de Alberto Núñez Feijóo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Feijóo y Abascal evitan el choque en la campaña del 29-N: “El cambio está por encima del PP”
items.description: El presidente de Castilla y León, el popular Alfonso Fernández Mañueco, y el vicepresidente primero, Carlos Pollán, de Vox, exhibieron sintonía este martes en una comparecencia conjunta para presentar su pacto de Presupuestos para 2027. En las primeras cuentas tras el acuerdo de Gobierno con la extrema derecha que incluyó la polémica “prioridad nacional” de los españoles frente a los extranjeros, la preferencia de los nacionales sobre los inmigrantes no apareció por ninguna parte . Mañueco y Pollán aparcaron las diferencias y se esforzaron en cumplir con la estrategia de “gobernar con Vox sin dar miedo” que los populares, según fuentes de este partido, se han impuesto en las comunidades autónomas que han hecho de avanzadilla de los acuerdos con la extrema derecha. La imagen de complicidad entre los dos partidos en Castilla y León no es una excepción. Los líderes de PP y Vox, Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal, han sincronizado la estrategia y están evitando el choque en la precampaña hacia el 29-N. “El cambio está por encima del PP”, enfatizó ayer el líder de los populares, que ya no reclama un Gobierno en solitario. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dimite la cúpula de la Fundación Complutense, tercer motín en un año en el campus más grande de España
items.description: El equipo directivo de la Fundación General de la Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM) presentó el pasado 6 de octubre su “dimisión irrevocable” al rector Joaquín Goyache en una carta a la que ha accedido este diario. Abandonan sus cargos por voluntad propia la directora general, la subdirectora de Investigación e Innovación y el subdirector académico de esta institución centrada en la gestión de la investigación, la formación y la transferencia del conocimiento de la UCM. Entre los motivos que aseguran han precipitado su dimisión está la forma en la que, dicen, se han traspasado las “funciones, procedimientos y personal” de su entidad al vicerrectorado de Investigación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ni salir de casa ni conseguir empleo: las listas de espera, una barrera para la independencia de miles de discapacitados
items.description: No contar con un certificado de discapacidad puede condicionar la vida de una persona de muchas maneras. Miguel Ángel Pardo Martín dejó de hacer una de las cosas que más disfrutaba: recorrer las calles de Madrid. Desde que sufrió un tercer ictus en enero de 2026, quedó con secuelas en el habla y en la movilidad y, desde entonces, perdió independencia. Al tener una incapacidad absoluta permanente, ya no puede salir solo de su piso en Villaviciosa de Odón y depende casi totalmente de un scooter eléctrico para moverse. “Antes iba al centro, pero ahora ya no puedo porque hay que coger el autobús y luego un metro. Ya he dejado de venir a Madrid por libertad”, explica el hombre de 67 años modulando con cierta dificultad. Las pocas veces que sale, lo hace para ir a una consulta médica. “Si tenemos que ir a cualquier sitio en el coche, lo tengo que dejar en el laboratorio o en el hospital, y ponerme a dar vueltas para poder aparcarlo”, explica su esposa, Montserrat López Espejo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El mercado de la artrosis: un tercio de los pacientes de Quirón que huyen de la saturación en Madrid son de traumatología
items.description: La reciente polémica por la alteración en la lista de espera del Ramón y Cajal de Madrid ha dejado al desnudo la enorme presión que soporta el servicio afectado: la traumatología. Este gran hospital, que atiende a más de 600.000 madrileños, no da abasto para atender la fuerte demanda de pacientes, sobre todo personas mayores con problemas de desgaste en huesos y articulaciones. No se trata de un caso aislado. La mayoría de hospitales públicos madrileños deriva pacientes de traumatología en una misma dirección: los cinco hospitales gestionados en la red pública por dos grandes empresas privadas, Ribera y Quirón. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las resistencias bacterianas disparan el impétigo infantil y dejan obsoletas las pomadas más usadas
items.description: “ Aixa tiene impétigo . El viernes la llevamos al pediatra porque tenía una pequeña lesión en la nariz y le recetó una pomada antibiótica. Hoy lunes tenía que volver al colegio, pero no lo hemos visto claro porque la lesión ha crecido. Así que hemos vuelto al centro de salud y esta vez le han dado un antibiótico oral. En fin, que aunque no sea grave, como es muy contagioso y un rollo patatero, nos quedamos más tranquilos si lo sabéis todos”. Alba Pascual escribió este mensaje en el grupo de WhatsApp de la clase de su hija mayor, en un colegio del barrio de La Sagrera (Barcelona). Era diciembre de 2024 y entonces pensó que la niña, que ahora cursa sexto de primaria, “había tenido mala suerte” con esta infección de la piel causada por las bacterias Staphylococcus aureus o Streptococcus pyogenes que provoca la aparición de manchas rojas, ampollas y llagas, generalmente en torno a la boca o la nariz. Lo que desconocía entonces esta profesora de secundaria de 40 años era que el incremento de casos como el de Aixa preocupaba desde hacía un tiempo a pediatras, dermatólogos e investigadores. Seguir leyendo

items.title: NBA, Roland Garros y, ahora, el Mundial de fútbol: el deporte en directo se convierte en la gran apuesta de las plataformas de ‘streaming’ en España
items.description: Desde hace varias temporadas, existe una tendencia clara (y paradójica) en las plataformas de streaming españolas: apostar por contenidos y formas de monetización propios de la televisión tradicional en abierto . Además de incorporar publicidad y formatos de entretenimiento clásicos como Operación Triunfo , compañías como Prime Video, HBO Max y Apple TV abren su catálogo a la emisión de competiciones deportivas en vivo. Netflix ha anunciado este martes que ha adquirido los derechos exclusivos para España y Andorra de los 104 partidos del Mundial de fútbol 2030 . Se trata de una cobertura que este verano se encargó una plataforma especializada en deporte como DAZN y cuyo saltó a Netflix refrenda el cambio de rumbo de las grandes marcas de entretenimiento a la carta. items.title: ‘VisionQuest’ lleva al psicólogo a un androide: “Asumen que Marvel es una máquina infernal, pero es de las experiencias más colaborativas e imaginativas”
items.description: Es un bicho raro. Trabaja en una sencilla taberna de Edimburgo. No tiene amigos y tampoco enemigos. Vive el presente sin saber demasiado de su pasado. Y las líneas diplomáticas de su traje están formadas por ceros y unos. Es una criatura contradictoria que, pese a estar fabricada con metal vibranio, se siente más humana que máquina. O no. Porque si hay algo que le caracteriza es su constante cuestionamiento vital: tiene más dudas que certezas, más preguntas que respuestas. El nuevo Visión que Marvel presenta en VisionQuest es un tipo capaz de hacer millones de simulaciones en un nanosegundo al que no le vendría mal pasar por un terapeuta. Y cuyas relaciones familiares —un hijo, un padre— son clave en la nueva serie, cierre de la trilogía que comenzó con La Bruja Escarlata y Visión y continuó con Agatha, ¿quién si no? Drama, ciencia ficción y humor se mezclan en ocho capítulos que no dan respiro. Y que permiten al espectador, por primera vez, adentrarse en la mente de un superhéroe que abandona los rayos láser para centrarse en lo importante. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Gastrificación’, la invasión de las mismas comidas y restaurantes en todas partes
items.description: Recorres el centro de una ciudad cualquiera en busca de un sitio donde comer. Nunca habías pisado esas calles, pero el ambiente te resulta familiar. Quizás sean las firmas de ropa que ya conoces de memoria, la publicidad de los refrescos de siempre salpicando las marquesinas o las cadenas de comida rápida que vas encontrando a tu paso. Quizás sean los restaurantes que, desde fuera, se adivinan “para turistas”, o que te cuesta encontrar una cafetería o un bar que no utilice la palabra auténtico como un reclamo vacío . items.title: Dentro de la despensa del ‘boomer’ español: vino, conservas y jamón. “Es más fácil cambiar de religión que de hábitos alimenticios”
items.description: Si abre usted la nevera o mira la despensa de un boomer español —por simplificar, de alguien que está en sus sesenta — encontrará vino, cervezas, embutidos, salmón, patés, conservas y aceite, como si fuera una cesta de Navidad. Al menos, en mayor medida que si abre otra nevera cualquiera. “En estos hogares se compran más bebidas, más conservas y más embutidos que la media”, dice Marta Cerón, de Nielsen, tras consultar un panel de 12.000 hogares representativos de todo el país. En su lista también aparecen el café, el azúcar, las aceitunas y la sobrasada. “Podríamos decir que son categorías… ¿menos saludables?”, apunta. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Marrakech Comedy Festival dévoile sa bande-annonce avant sa diffusion le 16 octobre
items.description: La plateforme Disney+ a révélé la bande-annonce officielle du Marrakech Comedy Festival, dont le gala francophone sera diffusé en exclusivité le 16 octobre 2026. Présentée par Malik Bentalha, cette première édition met à l’honneur une nouvelle génération d’humoristes dans le cadre du Palais des Congrès de Marrakech. Le rire marocain et francophone s’invite sur Disney+. La plateforme a dévoilé la bande-annonce du Marrakech Comedy Festival, dont le gala francophone sera disponible en exclusivité à partir du 16 octobre. Captée en juin dernier au Palais des Congrès de Marrakech, cette première édition ambitionne de faire de la ville ocre un rendez-vous incontournable de l’humour francophone et arabophone. Imaginé et présenté par Malik Bentalha, le festival réunit des humoristes aux univers variés, entre talents émergents et artistes déjà reconnus sur la scène du stand-up. Pour le maître de cérémonie et directeur artistique de l’événement, cette diffusion constitue une nouvelle étape après une première édition marquée par l’énergie du public et la diversité des performances. « Voir la première édition du Marrakech Comedy Festival arriver sur Disney+ est une immense fierté » , souligne Malik Bentalha, qui évoque également une réussite collective et un souvenir marquant vécu sur la scène marrakchie. Une scène ouverte à une nouvelle génération Parmi les artistes présents dans ce gala figurent Meryem Benoua, Tom Baldetti, Paul de Saint Sernin, Youness Hanifi, Nordine Ganso, Léopold Le Marchand, Hugo Le Van et Sarah Lélé. Plusieurs surprises sont également annoncées au fil du programme. À travers cette programmation, le Marrakech Comedy Festival entend mettre en lumière la diversité des écritures comiques et favoriser les rencontres entre les scènes marocaine et francophone. La captation promet aux abonnés de retrouver les performances au plus près de la scène, dans l’atmosphère du Palais des Congrès. Les galas francophone et arabophone seront également diffusés prochainement sur la télévision nationale. Produit par Karim Debbouze et Malik Bentalha et réalisé par Julien Faustino, le programme marque une nouvelle étape dans la visibilité du festival auprès du public international. The post Marrakech Comedy Festival dévoile sa bande-annonce avant sa diffusion le 16 octobre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Joint opposition flays move to ‘usurp KP govt mandate’
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A joint meeting of opposition parties on Tuesday demanded the immediate withdrawal of the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and called for respecting the democratic mandate of the people of the province. According to a statement issued after a meeting of the opposition parliamentary parties at Parliament House, the participants strongly condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the removal of its elected government, and the arrest of political leaders and workers. The meeting was chaired by NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai, and attended by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, PTI secretary general Salman Akram Raja and other opposition leaders. The statement said that Oct 11 would be remembered as a black day in Pakistan’s democratic history. It called the removal of the elected government in KP, the arrest of PTI leaders, including Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, and action against political workers contrary to the mandate given by the people of the province, and democratic values. The participants demanded that the fundamental rights of the arrested leaders and workers be protected and that the supremacy of the Constitution and the law be upheld, the statement said. According to the statement, Maulana Fazlur Rehman briefed the meeting on his negotiations with the government, saying the step in KP was taken despite the talks having been completed. The participants appreciated his role in promoting the democratic process, easing political tension and seeking to resolve issues through dialogue. The statement said questions were also raised at the meeting over what participants described as double standards in the government’s handling of Balochistan and KP. If the provinces faced law and order or constitutional problems, uniform principles should be applied to resolve them, it said, adding that dissolving an elected government or taking undemocratic action on the basis of political differences was not a solution. The rights of the people and the mandate of elected representatives in all provinces, including KP and Balochistan, must be respected equally, the statement said. Instead of unilateral decisions, the statement added, a comprehensive national strategy against terrorism should be formulated in consultation with all relevant stakeholders, and the province should be given the resources it needs. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: US may have ‘gone too far’ in targeting Iran leaders
items.description: OHIO: US President Donald Trump said that the United States “might have gone too far” in targeting Iran’s leadership. “We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don’t know who the hell we’re dealing with any more,” he said during a campaign rally in Ohio, according to Middle East Eye. “Nobody wants to be the president of Iran,” he added, claiming that potential candidates did not want to take up the position. Trump made this remark despite Masoud Pezeshkian being Iran’s president since July 2024. “We’re having a hard time figuring out who the hell to deal with, to be honest with you. I think we went too far,” the US president said. Trump says he doesn’t believe China, Russia are helping Iran Meanwhile, Trump said on Monday that he does not believe that China and Russia are helping Iran, adding that they have “too much to lose.” Trump has faced pressure over reports that Chinese and Russian entities have supplied Iran with intelligence for attacks on US troops. Responding to comments that China and Russia are helping Iran, Trump said in a post on Truth Social: “If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!” Trump said in July that he did not believe China and Russia were selling weapons to Iran, warning that “it would be very bad for them” if they did. China and Russia both maintain strong ties with Iran but have refrained from getting directly involved in the Middle East war, which began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28. Since the outbreak of the war, Russia has sent humanitarian aid to Iran, but has otherwise not officially announced any concrete assistance. The Kremlin has denied US media reports claiming that Moscow passed sensitive intelligence to Iran, including the locations of US warships and aircraft in the region. China has sharply condemned US and Israeli strikes while also criticising Iranian attacks on Gulf states and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz. China has previously supplied Iran with drones as well as equipment that can be used for both civilian and military purposes. Beijing has denied reports that the country’s top semiconductor firm, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, has sent chipmaking tools to Iran. China and Russia have also been accused of helping Iran circumvent international sanctions targeting its oil sales. Trump has frequently taken a more deferential tone toward Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin than he has toward some of Washington’s own allies, saying that they must be respected as the leaders of major world powers. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: Houthis warn of ‘painful’ response as Saudis strike Yemen fuel sites
items.description: • Coalition says struck sites ‘supported Houthi missile, drone operations’ • Aerial threat alerts issued for Riyadh, Eastern Province; blasts heard near Dhahran • Trump warns rebels; Erdogan pledges support for Riyadh RIYADH: Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen on Tuesday, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations. Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s Eastern Province and Riyadh. Residents in the Eastern Province received alerts saying the area faced a “hostile aerial threat” before being told shortly afterwards that the danger had passed. Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. There was no immediate confirmation that the facility itself had been struck. The Saudi-led coalition said fragments from an intercepted projectile had fallen on a residential area in Dhahran. The developments marked a further escalation in the rapidly widening confrontation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis, who have stepped up missile and drone attacks on the kingdom over the past week. Earlier on Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had conducted military operations against “vital assets” used by the Houthis to sustain their war effort, Al Jazeera reported. Coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said the targets included the Al-Sabaha central station in Sanaa, underground fuel reserves and storage tanks, as well as energy facilities in Hodeidah, Sanaa and Dhamar. The coalition said the sites were being used to supply the Houthis’ missile and drone arsenal, posing threats to Saudi Arabia, airports, ports and commercial shipping in the Red Sea. “The operation aims to neutralise the Houthis’ capabilities that threaten the Kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea, and waterways,” the coalition said. Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that the Saudi-led coalition had struck a Yemen Petroleum Company facility on the western outskirts of Sanaa. An AFP correspondent in the Yemeni capital reported hearing an explosion after the coalition had earlier issued an evacuation warning for civilians near the site — its first such order for Sanaa since the war flared up again. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree also said the site had “no military value”, while the group warned that any further Saudi strikes would draw retaliation against targets in the kingdom. The Houthis identified Riyadh’s international airport, an oil refinery in the capital and Aramco facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia among potential targets, and renewed warnings to workers to stay away from sites that could be attacked. Saudi Arabia vows response The Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the kingdom would not allow threats to its security or to freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait. It warned that the Houthis would “face the consequences of their crimes and repeated attacks” on Saudi airports, holy cities and economic facilities. Saudi Arabia also faced continuing attacks on Tuesday, with the coalition saying it had intercepted three drones north of Riyadh. Blasts had also been heard over the Saudi capital late on Monday, when the coalition said it intercepted a Houthi missile and the group claimed another attack on Riyadh airport. Trump, Erdogan weigh in US President Donald Trump spoke to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday and later told reporters that the Houthis were “behaving very badly”. He also accused the group of trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the Nov 3 US midterm elections and warned that he would “never forget” their attacks on Saudi Arabia. Trump said he might ask Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to intervene in support of Saudi interests. Earlier on Tuesday, Erdogan told the Sa­­u­­di crown prince that Ankara would stand by the kingdom, according to the Turkish presidency, though no details were given on any specific new line of support. Turkiye and Pakistan signed a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia this summer, although Ankara still requires parliamentary approval to implement its commitments under the agreement. Senior Houthi official Mohammed al-Bukhaiti said the group would target American interests in the region if Washington joined the war. He said the attacks on Saudi targets were intended to signal to the Saudi leadership that it could no longer wage war in Yemen “from a safe position”. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: Cameroun: le président Paul Biya fixe les priorités du budget 2027, sans préciser le calendrier électoral
items.description: Au Cameroun, Paul Biya fixe le cap du prochain budget de l'État, mais laisse planer le doute sur le calendrier électoral. Dans une lettre circulaire datée de lundi 12 octobre 2026 et consacrée à la préparation du budget 2027, le président camerounais a indiqué les axes prioritaires de son gouvernement pour l'année prochaine. La rigueur et le patriotisme économique y occupent une bonne place. Mais les observateurs ont noté qu'il n'y a pas, dans ce document de 24 pages, d'engagement clair concernant la tenue des élections municipales et législatives, déjà reportées plusieurs fois et attendues pour l'an prochain.

items.title: Révolution sportive au Burkina Faso : Gouverneurs au premier rang, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré impose l’obligation de résultats
items.description: Face à la dégradation de la santé publique chez les jeunes et au déclin des disciplines sportives nationales, le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a réuni le lundi 12 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou les gouverneurs de région et les responsables du monde sportif. En instaurant la « Ligue de la Souveraineté », le Chef de l'État entend utiliser la compétition sportive comme un levier central de la Révolution, visant à éradiquer la consommation de stupéfiants en milieu scolaire et à forger une jeunesse saine, consciente et patriote. C'est un diagnostic sans complaisance qu'a dressé le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, lors de sa rencontre de cadrage avec les gouverneurs de région. Face à la propagation de la drogue, du tabagisme et des alcools frelatés qui ravagent les lycées, collèges et milieux d'apprentissage, le Chef de l'État réaffirme qu'« on ne peut pas construire une Nation avec une jeunesse qui est malade ». Alors que la douane intercepte quotidiennement des cargaisons de produits illicites camouflés, les autorités ont décidé de changer de stratégie : plutôt que de se limiter à des interdictions formelles, l'État mise sur la mise en compétition systématique de la jeunesse par le sport pour préserver sa santé physique et mentale. La création de la Ligue de la Souveraineté s'inscrit au cœur du processus de refondation patriotique. Pour le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, l'esprit révolutionnaire exige de rompre avec la routine et de « casser la rouille » pour rebâtir un système sportif moribond. L'objectif stratégique consiste à doter chaque région d'une identité sportive forte, capable de susciter l'attachement des populations et de créer une émulation saine à travers tout le pays. Commençant par le football masculin senior, le dispositif s'étendra progressivement aux équipes féminines, aux petites catégories et à l'ensemble des disciplines sportives telles que l'athlétisme, le cyclisme, la boxe et la lutte. Dans ce nouveau schéma territorial, les gouverneurs de région se voient confier une mission de coordination de premier ordre. Il leur incombe désormais d'organiser les tournois régionaux de détection, de recruter les encadreurs techniques et de constituer les sélections représentatives. Avertissant contre tout relâchement ou tentative de sabotage d'ici l'échéance de fin décembre, le Président du Faso a prévenu qu'un suivi rigoureux sera assuré par des observateurs dédiés, soulignant que la réussite de cette politique dans les provinces conditionnera l'évaluation des premiers responsables régionaux. L’article Révolution sportive au Burkina Faso : Gouverneurs au premier rang, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré impose l'obligation de résultats est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Meurtre de Daouda Traoré : Le procureur requiert la prison à vie contre Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kaboré
items.description: Programmé depuis le 8 juin 2026 et plusieurs fois reporté, le procès de Sayouba Sankara et de Boukary Kaboré s'est finalement tenu le 12 octobre 2026 devant la justice. Poursuivis pour l'assassinat de Daouda Traoré commis le 26 mars 2025 au secteur n°2 (Médina-Coura), le vendeur de véhicules et son complice, un homme de tenue, ont reconnu l'intégralité des faits à la barre. Face à ce crime commis pour dépouiller la victime venue verser l'argent d'un achat automobile, le procureur a requis la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité à l'encontre des deux accusés. Les faits remontent à la journée du 26 mars 2025. Ce jour-là, Daouda Traoré s'est rendu à moto au bureau de Sayouba Sankara, un vendeur de véhicules avec lequel il avait conclu un accord pour l'achat d'une voiture, afin de lui verser la somme convenue. Ignorant qu'il s'agissait de son dernier jour sur terre, l'acheteur est tombé dans un piège. Avec la complicité de Boukary Kaboré, un homme de tenue, le commerçant a froidement assassiné Daouda Traoré. Tard dans la nuit, les deux complices ont jeté le corps de la victime au cimetière du secteur n°17, avant d'incendier sa motocyclette à la sortie de Bobo-Dioulasso, sur la route de Ouagadougou. Initialement programmée le 8 juin 2026, l'ouverture de la procédure judiciaire avait été reportée à plusieurs reprises. Les deux mis en cause exigeaient en effet de bénéficier de l'assistance d'un avocat avant de répondre des faits d'assassinat reprochés. L'État a ainsi mis à leur disposition un défenseur pour assurer leur protection juridique. Après ces retards successifs, le procès s'est formellement ouvert le 12 octobre 2026. À la barre du tribunal, Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kaboré ont reconnu les faits et ont avoué avoir décidé de « limer » leur victime. Interrogés par le procureur sur la signification exacte de ce terme, les deux hommes ont fini par admettre qu'il s'agissait de lui ôter la vie. À l'issue des débats, estimant la gravité des faits établie, le procureur a requis la peine de prison à vie à l'encontre des deux accusés. L’article Meurtre de Daouda Traoré : Le procureur requiert la prison à vie contre Sayouba Sankara et Boukary Kaboré est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Football burkinabè : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré veut briser le monopole Ouaga-Bobo pour révéler tous les talents du territoire
items.description: Jusqu'alors étouffé par des gestions associatives opaques et le monopole des clubs de Ouagadougou et Bobo-Dioulasso, le sport burkinabè entame une mue historique. Lors d'un échange direct avec les acteurs du monde sportif et en présence d'anciens internationaux tels que Charles Kaboré, Alain Traoré et Adama Guira, le Président du Faso a annoncé un cadre législatif novateur pour transformer les clubs en sociétés sportives, mettre fin aux passe-droits et instaurer une stricte culture du mérite. Pointant du doigt les défaillances structurelles des fédérations et des clubs traditionnels, le gouvernement critique la situation où l'État finance la quasi-totalité des charges (déplacements, hébergements, primes, subventions) sans disposer d'un droit de regard opérationnel. Jusqu'à présent, toute tentative de contrôle se heurtait au chantage à la suspension par les instances internationales pour cause d'ingérence étatique. La future loi sur le sport mettra un terme au modèle associatif classique en imposant le passage à des sociétés sportives structurées , soumises à une rigueur comptable absolue et au contrôle de l'utilisation des deniers publics. S'adressant à la fois aux gouverneurs et aux cadres techniques, le Chef de l'État a fermement proscrit les mauvaises pratiques qui gangrènent les sélections, notamment le monnayage des places de joueurs contre des pourcentages sur contrat. L'intégration dans les équipes régionales devra s'effectuer exclusivement sur la base du talent et des performances sur le terrain, sans égard pour les filiations ou le rang social. L'arbitrage et la gestion des matchs feront également l'objet d'une surveillance renforcée pour garantir la transparence totale des compétitions. Pour réussir cette transformation, l'État associe étroitement d'anciennes gloires du football burkinabè — à l'instar de Charles Kaboré, nommé ambassadeur pour le sport, d'Alain Traoré et d'Adama Guira — afin d'apporter leur expérience du haut niveau et de veiller à la déontologie du projet. De plus, la Ligue de la Souveraineté brise l'hégémonie historique des centres urbains de Ouagadougou et Bobo-Dioulasso en offrant une vitrine aux jeunes talents issus des 13 régions du pays, créant ainsi un vivier élargi pour alimenter les futures équipes nationales. items.title: Modèle économique du sport burkinabè lancé par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré : 200 000 FCFA de salaire minimum et près de 1 000 emplois créés
items.description: Pour mettre fin à la précarité dramatique qui frappe les athlètes locaux, le gouvernement burkinabè fixe désormais à 200 000 FCFA le salaire mensuel minimum de chaque joueur engagé dans la nouvelle Ligue de la Souveraineté, assorti d'une affiliation à la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS). Reposant sur la création de sociétés sportives régionales, ce projet permettra de générer près de 1 000 emplois directs dès sa phase de lancement, grâce à un mécanisme de financement combinant subvention initiale de l'État, réallocation des budgets communaux et soutien obligatoire du secteur privé. Révélant que de nombreux athlètes évoluent aujourd'hui sans percevoir le moindre revenu décent, le Chef de l'État impose une revalorisation salariale d'envergure. Au sein de la Ligue de la Souveraineté, chaque joueur percevra au minimum 200 000 FCFA par mois et bénéficiera d'une déclaration formelle à la CNSS. Les cadres d'encadrement technique percevront quant à eux une rémunération supérieure d'au moins 50 % à ce plancher. Avec 20 équipes régionales composées de 30 joueurs chacune, le dispositif génère immédiatement 740 à près de 1 000 emplois directs financés sous forme de contrats professionnels. Afin d'assurer la viabilité de ces nouvelles sociétés sportives régionales, l'État prendra en charge l'intégralité du budget de fonctionnement pour la première année de compétition. Par la suite, le relais sera assuré par une clé de répartition budgétaire locale : une part obligatoire des budgets de chaque commune et du Conseil régional sera désormais affectée au sport, mettant fin aux colloques et réunions jugés inefficaces. De plus, les gouverneurs s'appuieront sur une contribution « volontaire mais obligatoire » des opérateurs économiques et des chambres de commerce régionales. Sur le plan national, le Ministère des Finances désignera 20 grandes entreprises publiques et privées pour sponsoriser directement les 20 formations du championnat. Outre l'aspect financier, le gouvernement a engagé la commande de cars de transport dédiés à chaque équipe pour sécuriser leurs déplacements régionaux, avec l'appui de l'armée si nécessaire. Enfin, la construction et la réhabilitation d'infrastructures sportives aux normes professionnelles seront confiées à un consortium d'entreprises spécialisées afin de permettre, à terme, des compétitions en aller-retour dans l'ensemble des provinces. L’article Modèle économique du sport burkinabè lancé par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré : 200 000 FCFA de salaire minimum et près de 1 000 emplois créés est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Commémoration du 15 octobre 2026 : Le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple instaure la journée continue jusqu’à 14h
items.description: Conformément à la loi n° 001-2026/ALT du 09 janvier 2026, la journée du 15 octobre est dédiée à la commémoration et au recueillement au Burkina Faso. Par un communiqué officiel, le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple informe l'ensemble des travailleurs et employeurs des secteurs public et privé que les horaires de travail du 15 octobre 2026 sont réaménagés de 7 heures 30 minutes à 14 heures sur toute l'étendue du territoire national. À l'attention des acteurs du monde professionnel, le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple a rendu public un communiqué portant sur l'organisation de la journée du 15 octobre 2026. Cette décision découle de l'application de la loi n° 001-2026/ALT du 09 janvier 2026, instituant des jours chômés et payés ainsi que des journées de commémoration et de recueillement au Burkina Faso. À ce titre, la date du 15 octobre est formellement établie comme une journée de commémoration et de recueillement. Pour l'ensemble des travailleurs et employeurs des secteurs public et privé, le temps de travail fait l'objet d'un réajustement spécifique sur tout le territoire national. Lors de la journée du 15 octobre 2026, les heures de service sont fixées de 7 heures 30 minutes à 14 heures. Afin de garantir la continuité des prestations essentielles, des mesures d'adaptation sont prévues pour certaines structures. Au sein des services ou unités à activités permanentes, les responsables d'équipe sont chargés d'organiser la prise de relais et les tours de garde nécessaires pour assurer la fourniture des prestations en dehors de la plage horaire réglementaire de 7 h 30 à 14 h 00. L’article Commémoration du 15 octobre 2026 : Le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple instaure la journée continue jusqu'à 14h est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: PTI seeks production orders for nine ‘detained’ MNAs
items.description: ISLAMABAD/PESHAWAR: The PTI has urged National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq to issue production orders for its nine detained MNAs ahead of the National Assembly and Senate sessions scheduled for Tuesday. In a letter to NA Speaker, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that the nine MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the 30th session starting on Tuesday. The lawmakers include Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry, Muhammad Jamal Ahsan Khan, Mian Ghous Muhammad, Sanaullah Khan Mastikhel, Dawar Khan Kundi, Junaid Akbar, Amjad Ali Khan, Fazal Muhammad Khan and Adil Khan Bazai. The PTI chief whip urged the speaker to take immediate notice of the matter and issue production orders to ensure the detained lawmakers’ attendance in the House. Afridi’s brother, speaker’s cousin move high court to trace their relatives CM, speaker’s family move PHC The brother of non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi approached the Peshawar High Court to trace his whereabouts, while Waqar Ahmad Khan, a cousin of KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, also filed a petition before the court seeking similar relief. The federal government had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on October 11. On the same day, the PTI claimed that Mr Afridi, along with some of his cabinet ministers and party leaders, had been abducted. The next day, officials, however, confirmed that Mr Afridi and some of his cabinet members were in preventative custody. Muhammad Amir, Mr Afridi’s brother, filed a petition in the PHC, seeking multiple directives for the respondents, including the KP inspector general of police, Peshawar capital city police officer and others, to immediately take all lawful and effective measures to trace and recover his brother and, if he was found to be in custody, produce him before the high court so that the legality of his detention could be examined in accordance with Article 199(1)(b)(i) of the Constitution. The petition was filed through senior counsel Bashir Khan Wazir. He contended that the impugned detention and disappearance of the abductee were “wholly illegal, unlawful, without lawful authority and of no legal effect”, as the respondents had “failed to disclose any lawful order, warrant, abduction order or other legal authority under which the abductee was taken into custody”. Separately, in his petition, KP speaker’s cousin Waqar Ahmad Khan states: “That, on 11.10.2026, at approximately 7:00pm, the detenue was allegedly abducted by certain unknown, armed and masked individuals from the premises of the Provincial Assembly of KP, Peshawar, in the presence of CCPO Peshawar. The precise sequence of events, the identities of the persons involved, and the circumstances in which the detenue was taken away require immediate verification through the relevant official record, eyewitness accounts, and other available evidence.” Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: Carnet noir pour le cyclisme burkinabè : L’emblématique animateur El Hadj Boukaré Tiemtoré, dit « 14 », s’est éteint
items.description: Le monde des médias et du sport burkinabè est plongé dans le deuil à la suite du décès d'El Hadj Boukaré Tiemtoré, dit « 7+7=14 » ou « Ladji 14 », survenu dans la matinée du mardi 13 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou des suites de maladie. Ancienne gloire du cyclisme reconvertie avec succès dans le commentaire sportif en langue mooré à la radio Horizon FM et sur les routes de la petite reine, cet homme d'exception s'éteint à quelques jours seulement du départ de la 37ᵉ édition du Tour du Faso, laissant un vide immense au sein de la presse et de la grande famille du vélo. C'est avec une vive émotion que la Direction générale de la radio Horizon FM et la Fédération burkinabè de cyclisme (FBC) ont annoncé la disparition d'El Hadj Boukaré Tiemtoré dans la nuit du lundi 12 au mardi 13 octobre 2026. Affaibli par la maladie au cours des derniers jours, celui que les auditeurs surnommaient affectueusement « 14 » ou « 7+7=14 » s'est éteint à Ouagadougou. Figure populaire et chaleureuse de « la radio du peuple », il aura marqué plusieurs décennies du paysage audiovisuel national par sa proximité avec les auditeurs et son talent inégalé de chroniqueur sportif en langue mooré. Avant de devenir la voix incontournable des événements sportifs, Boukaré Tiemtoré a d'abord été un coureur engagé. Il s'était illustré sur le vélo aux toutes premières heures du Tour du Faso, écrivant ainsi les pionnières pages de l'histoire du cyclisme national. Une fois sa carrière sur route achevée, il avait troqué son guidon contre le micro pour se reconvertir en chroniqueur et animateur de choc. Ses commentaires vivants et passionnés lors des compétitions nationales ont bercé des générations d'amoureux du vélo. Au-delà de ses interventions radiophoniques, El Hadj Boukaré Tiemtoré s'était imposé comme un promoteur engagé en créant le « Grand Prix 14 », une compétition devenue au fil des ans le rendez-vous traditionnel d'ouverture de la saison cycliste au Burkina Faso. Sa disparition survient tragiquement à seulement quelques jours du premier coup de pédale de la 37ᵉ édition du Tour du Faso 2026, un événement auquel il a consacré l'essentiel de sa vie. Alors que le programme des obsèques doit être communiqué ultérieurement, la FBC, la rédaction d'Horizon FM et l'ensemble de la presse sportive saluent la mémoire d'un compagnon de route d'exception et présentent leurs condoléances à sa famille éplorée. items.title: Will China beat the US in AI?
items.description: IN China, people are being paid to fold clothes, wipe tables, and open microwave doors. Wearing virtual reality headsets and exoskeletons, they repeat the movements hundreds of times so humanoid robots can learn them. Across China, similar centres have people performing other painfully ordinary tasks. The work looks mundane, but it produces precious data. It may seem like an odd way to begin a story about geopolitics, but like this piece, it offers im­­portant clues about who is better placed to ‘win’ the AI race — China or the US? The winner will have a much larger say in the next world order. Donald Trump insists America must win the AI race, a contest his administration has likened to the Cold War’s ‘space race’. The analogy is attractive, but Michael Kratsios, Trump’s science advi­ser, later conceded the obvious problem. Unlike the race to the moon, this one has no finish line. On the conventional scoreboard, the US rem­ains formidable. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index counts 59 notable American models in 2025 against China’s 35. US private AI investment exceeded China’s 23 times over, though this understates Chinese spending through government funds. Yet the report says the model performance gap has “effectively closed”, as of March 2026, the leading US model was ahead by just 2.7 per cent. Pakistan does not need to win the AI race. It needs to win from AI. Frontier models are not the only measure of success. China may be building its advantage by pushing AI into the physical economy. In March, the US China Economic and Security Review Commission ‘warned’ of a reinforcing lo­­­op in China. Cheap, open models spread into fa­­c­­to­r­ies, logistics, and robotics. Their use generates specialised real-world data, which then imp­roves the models. That could create an advantage proprietary American systems may struggle to mat­ch, even if they remain stronger on benchmarks. Most importantly, China had classified data as a factor of production in 2020. Factories are paid for access to workers wearing cameras and sensors, while others earn money performing household tasks to train robots. On the flip side, America’s AI boom grew out of an internet economy built on years of accumulated online content and behavioural data, where major platforms are accused of “vast surveillance” by the FTC, with users having little control over their data’s use. I am not suggesting China has a better privacy regime. It does not. The point is that China is producing, pricing, and feeding data back into industry, building an ecosystem that could give it an immense edge over the US. And it already has the machinery. China had more than two million industrial robots operating by 2024 and installed 354,000 in 2025 alone. According to the International Federation of Robotics, China accounted for 59pc of new industrial robot installations worldwide in 2025. The real advantage may, therefore, be the ecosystem itself, ie, factories produce robots, robots produce data, data improves AI, and AI improves factories. Then comes energy, as I argued earlier in these pages. The International Energy Agency (IEA) expects data centre electricity use to nearly double to 950 terawatt-hours by 2030. Whoever can expand reliable, affordable power fastest will have an edge in building the AI ecosystem. In the US, data centres are expected to account for nearly half of electricity demand growth to the end of the decade, while natural gas supplies more than 40pc of their electricity. Grid delays are pushing developers towards on-site gas generation. But the IEA says ensuring reliable supply requires generating capacity 30pc to 70pc above demand, while turbine shortages may undermine hopes of getting power faster. To its advantage, China accounts for around 85pc of global solar supply chain production capacity and 80pc of lithium-ion battery capacity. It added nearly 500 gigawatts of renewable capacity in 2025 alone. The idea isn’t to romanticise the figurative ‘Chinese model’, considering they still use coal to supply nearly 70pc of the electricity used by Chinese data centres. But their advantage is clear. China manufactures much of the machinery needed to generate and store the next unit of electricity. However, China still faces weaknesses. It depends on foreign technology across parts of the semiconductor chain, while restrictions on advanced memory are raising domestic chip costs. Chinese firms are nevertheless developing alternatives to Nvidia, seeking to make AI deployment more affordable and reduce dependence on American hardware. The US retains substantial advantages in frontier research, Nvidia’s computing ecosystem and capital, but China is building more of the hardware and software needed for its own ecosystem. The contest is also moving beyond the two countries. America’s AI Action Plan explicitly seeks to export full-stack US technology packages, including hardware, models, software and standards, whereas China is pushing open models and a competing international architecture. To summarise, if I had to pick a likely winner in the figurative AI race, I would lean towards China. Its advantage may lie in how effectively it turns AI into industrial strength and economic productivity. But the obvious question remains: Where does that leave Pakistan? Pakistan should resist that pressure to choose sides and rethink what it means to become a regional AI leader. Competing in frontier chips, foundation models and vast data centres requires an industrial base we lack. Our scarce resources should go where they can make the greatest difference. As I argued in ‘Pakistan’s AI checklist’, published in this paper in June, we need reliable power, computing capacity, local hosting for sensitive data, skilled people, local datasets, and rules that protect rights. We should use global tools where they help and build our own capacity where dependence leaves us vulnerable. The purpose of this investment must be clear. I have said this earlier as well. Pakistan does not need to win the AI race. It needs to win from AI. Helping farmers conserve water, teachers identify learning gaps, businesses become more productive, and public departments reduce waste would achieve more than another announcement about becoming an AI hub. China’s lesson is that technology becomes power when it translates into productivity. Our greatest risk is becoming little more than a market for systems built elsewhere, with too little capacity to shape how they serve us. The writer is the founder of Media Matters for Democracy. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: Moscow warns Tokyo's information gathering attempts will strain ties
items.description: Tokyo's attempts to use its correspondents in Russia to gather information will further strain Russia-Japan relations, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said in a statement on Tuesday. Imai Yuki, a Japanese correspondent who was detained on suspicion of espionage, has been transferred to Moscow and placed in custody, Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) said on Tuesday. The correspondent worked at the bureau of the Japanese newspaper Hokkaido Shimbun in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, the administrative center of the Sakhalin region. Imai is accused of espionage under Article 276 of the Russian Criminal Code, Zakharova said. "Tokyo's attempts to use its correspondents in Russia, who hold foreign journalist status, to gather information aimed at undermining our country's security are regrettable," Zakharova said. Given the overall decline in bilateral cooperation caused by the Japanese authorities' anti-Russian policies since the start of Russia's special military operation, as well as Tokyo's reluctance to heed Moscow's concerns regarding Japan's remilitarization policy, "we are forced to note that this development will further darken the atmosphere of Russia-Japan relations," she said, urging Tokyo to abandon hostile steps toward Russia.
